newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens starts facility management unit.
newsitem.headline: Siemens starts facility management unit.

text.p: German industrial group Siemens AG said on Tuesday it would start a facility management business expected to reach 250 million marks ($143 million) in sales in the 1997/98 business year.

After a start-up phase, Siemens Gebaeudemanagment und Services GmbH (SGM) would have 12 offices and 960 employees in Germany. It would become part of the group's building systems (ANL) business and take over activities already offered by ANL.
SGM would be run by Heinz Brunkhorst, who had managed Siemens' own facilities, and Karl-Otmar Giesler, who was hired from construction group Philip Holzmann AG.
SGM would seek to operate, modernise or modify plants for industrial companies. The unit could even form joint ventures with customers to build and run new facilities.
Siemens said the facility management market in Germany had an annual business volume of about seven billion marks.

In the six months to March 31, ANL reported sales rose six percent to 4.1 billion marks and orders fell four percent to 4.6 billion marks. In 1995/96, which ended September 31, it lost 102 million marks on sales of 9.4 billion marks. ($ = 1.746 German Marks)
